scope: Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core; standard 16-round 2–4-player multiplayer; base objective deck; marked expansions, optional variants and alternate modes excluded.
assessment: No material rules errors or important omissions found within the assigned scope. Quantities, timing, costs, destinations, scoring and exceptions in the snapshot are supported by the permitted primary sources. The unchanged reputation objective is supported by the explicitly permitted supplemental publisher example.

checked_claims.checked: The summary uses standard 16-space second-edition base/core multiplayer and consistently excludes marked expansion material and optional variants, including hiring when passing.
checked_claims.source_refs: Universal pp.2–6, 8–12, 16, 21, 29–30, 35–42; appendix expansion and objective-deck labels

checked_claims.checked: First player is random; family selection starts to their left; reputation 1.1; five initial servants, five starter tiles, four family members, two starter guests, five objectives, unused starters shuffled into casual deck, and all four family bonuses match.
One valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; unused servants are unavailable.

Players plus one double-sided monuments, at most one Estate monument; activity-to-monument suites remain in bag; six distinct eligible tiles with PR at most three, no Servants’ Hall or double-sided monument; duplicates stack and sort numerically.
Four seasons of three player-turn rounds plus courtship give twelve ordinary turns per player; courtship has no service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.
Village Fair 3 and 9; objectives 6; Builders’ Holiday 11; National Holiday 14; courtship 4, 8, 12, 16.
checked_claims.source_refs: Universal p.12 standard Alderley Hall board diagram, inspected as embedded PDF image

checked_claims.checked: Rotation, round event, ongoing effects, tile selection, exact invited gentry, service, favours, purchase, cleanup; only last player advances the round marker.
Full service refresh and discard recovery precede events and ongoing tiles, then £200 or market refresh and optional purchase; base hiring remains an activity.
Screening reputation is fixed after step 2 and before step 3; later spending does not invalidate tile or gentry eligibility. Gender, family, casual and prestige distinctions match.

Five increments per level; standard range 1.1–7.5; minimum protection; repeatable money and service actions cost two and three increments, market refresh costs four and is once per turn; overflow may be spent during a favour.
Positive favours resolve before negative ones; dismissal optional; a negative money payment must be funded, including borrowing when necessary, or the card/tile cannot be played.

Housekeeper and Brushing Room substitutions require absence of the relevant available common servant; underbutler substitutes for base male types even when available; unique servants cannot be recruited away.

Butler’s Room hires up to two non-underbutler servants or, after upgrading, one opponent common servant; hires and underbutler enter Expended Service; Pantry is the exclusive underbutler acquisition route.
Tile permits use of one Quarters servant each turn without reputation payment; Service Help moves one from Quarters to Available for three increments; Refresh Service returns all servants directly.
No hand limit; hand and discard both score; screening reveals only kept guests; rejected or dismissed guests go to matching deck bottoms; family cannot be dismissed.

checked_claims.topic: Base family and special guest favours
checked_claims.checked: Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady, Asquith Dowager, base Charles, Elizabeth and both base gossips match the stated favours and family/Fairchild VP.
Normal upgrades mandatory on first use; hybrids flip on every use and only face-up categories count; base hybrids and South Lawn family requirement match.
Monuments pay one reputation on later ordinary turns, including passes; Servants’ Hall expends one servant for its reputation transfer; Barn rewards hosted Estate activities.

Heritage doubles all favours including negatives; Queen doubles one selected favour; Lionheart draws the prestige guest with no personal service and doubles nonnegative favours; one-guest fixed counts and monument transitions match.

checked_claims.topic: Private Study, Main Library and West Terrace
checked_claims.checked: Study becomes Village-Fair ongoing income; Library draws objective then VP card with the stated family counts; base West Terrace uses butler and three family on both sides and upgraded prestige draw plus optional one-to-four dismissals.
checked_claims.source_refs: Universal pp.96, 99, 104; West Terrace PDF text checked directly

checked_claims.checked: Read all unmarked base improvement entries, including front/back requirements and unusual declining gentry counts; summary appropriately delegates individual unspecified tile values and favours to printed components.

checked_claims.topic: Market and Reserve costs, access and duplicate rules
checked_claims.checked: Normally one purchase; price modifiers and £100 minimum; Reserve £300 base; duplicate ownership prohibited by any means; all Reserve tiles public and purchasable without top-of-stack restriction.
Slide remaining tiles, stack duplicates, sort only newly drawn tiles; Service and later PR1 route to Reserve, excluding Largest Wine Cellar; refresh sets old Market aside until refill completes.
After the first three courtships Reserve movement precedes full refresh, new theme, anticlockwise first-player transfer and marker advance; older flowchart is explicitly incomplete.
checked_claims.source_refs: Universal p.23; Corrigendum p.2 Player Aid Note, both checked directly against PDFs

checked_claims.checked: Builders’ Holiday and Market Purchase VP benefit use the same unchanged market and existing prices, without sliding/refilling or refresh between purchases.

Five initial plus two at round 6 minus one at each courtship leaves three; extra objective acquisition increases final retained count; simultaneous discards shuffled and bottom-decked; tile objectives need ownership, not upgrade.
All ten printed benefit types, normal turn timing, immediate draw use, final post-courtship opportunity, multiple refresh cards, bottom-deck disposal, and retained VP choice match.
Fairchilds return first; seasonal theme VP includes negatives; ties award VP cards without Fairchild; final scoring sums four themes with repetitions and uses reputation level as tie-break.
All seven VP sources, reputation triangular values through 28, two VP per employed servant, wealth floor per £200, final Fairchild, and level-only tie-breaks match.

Checked all ten group objectives, two guest bonuses, five category bonuses, common-servant bonus, five servant-set objectives, four individual tiles, reputation, monument and wealth objectives against entries explicitly labelled Base.

Official localized base-rulebook example explicitly awards this objective for maximum reputation level shown by Max; p.7 identifies standard Max as seven. No older gameplay or seasonal flow was imported.
checked_claims.source_refs: Super Meeple publisher-fr-base-rules.pdf pp.7 and 14 and corresponding supplied text; Universal p.111

source_review.main_text: Read the supplied authoritative extracted text for core setup, play, detailed rules, full relevant FAQ, base gentry, improvement and VP entries, and all Base-labelled objectives.
source_review.pdf_checks: Read selected Universal PDF text directly for screening, seasonal flow, West Terrace and reputation objective; visually inspected embedded standard Alderley Hall board image for round positions; read both Corrigendum PDF pages directly.
source_review.supplemental_limit: Read only pp.7 and 14 relevant to the reputation objective in the supplied official French base rules text, and checked those PDF pages by direct extraction. No gameplay flow imported from this older source.

independence_statement: This was a fresh source-only audit. I read only the assigned summary snapshot and authorized authoritative rules/PDFs (plus the explicitly authorized French publisher base-rulebook material). I did not read questions, answer keys, reader responses, grades, previous audits or other QA evidence; did not communicate with readers; and did not edit or repair the summary.
